top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks (Katori, Ye) rest on one falsifiable idea, magic-wavelength trapping of many atoms so the light shift cancels for the clock transition, realized at about 1e-18 and reproduced and surpassed by several groups and species. The two-name allocation is uncontested and maps onto distinct steps (concept and first lattice spectroscopy, record accuracy and many-body control). The citation can be kept narrow and distinct from the 2005 and 2012 prizes. The magic-angle graphene trio is attractive but younger, its mechanism is unsettled, and the three-seat cut leaves out contested claimants, so it ranks second, ahead of no award.
